Definition
The fc detector circuit consists of the NE567 chip as shown in the simplified schematic.
Q1 is a common emitter switch and only allows the digital data out when the input from the fc detector is HIGH, meaning data is being transmitted.
The output of the amplifier is fed to Q1.
The information output on pin 7 and the reference output on pin 6 are applied to an op amp amplifier, IC2.
The capacitors and resistors connected to the demodulated output on pin 7 are a filter and used to ensure only HIGHs and LOWs are produced.
Pins 6 and 7 are the outputs. Pin 7 is the information output and pin 6 is the reference output.
Pins 8 and 9 set up the center frequency of the FM demodulator, fc (R and C inputs). R6 allows making adjustments.
The FSK signal is applied through R1, level control, to pins 2 and 3 of IC1. FSK is also applied to the fc detector circuit.
For the PLL demodulator, IC1, pin 10 is the power source and pin 1 is ground.
Definition
The FM demodulator circuit consists of the NE565 PLL FM demodulator, filter, IC2 amplifier and Q1 switch as shown in the simplified schematic.
The receiver circuit is contained on PC130-329 and consists of the components necessary to support the NE565 and NE567 PLL chips.
In this experiment, you will observe the operation and measure signals in a typical FSK receiver circuit.

R12 and R13 adjust the FM output symmetry.
R6, R8, and the CARRIER potentiometer (R16) adjust the DC voltages that are applied to the VCO for fc, fmin and fmax..........
R2 and R14 adjust the levels, R2 the digital input and R14 the FM output.
S1 is the manual control for transmitting data. In the CONTROL position, down, no data is transmitted.
Now, pick up the PC130-328 card and compare to the schematic.
The output is taken from pin 2, sine wave output, through C7 and R14, level control.
Pin 12 is used through R13 for symmetry adjustment. Pin 1 is not used.
Pins 4 and 5 are connected through R10, R11 and R12 for duty cycle adjustment, part of the symmetry control of the circuit.
The voltage from the switching circuit is applied to pin 8.
Definition
The FM modulator circuit consists of the ICL8038 VCO modulator chip as shown in the simplified schematic.
Definition
The switching circuit produces three DC voltages according to the information digital data and if data is to be transmitted.
Switch a closes, allowing Efmax to change the Efc voltage. The output of the VCO is fmax, the third frequency.
Switch b opens, Efmin does not effect the Efc voltage.
Switch d outputs +10 volts to switch a CONTROL input and switch c outputs 0 volts to switch b (R3 drops the +10 volts).
Switch c closing places a ground in the S1, R3, switch c circuit.
Definition
With a HIGH input from IC1, both switches c and d will close.
The 0 volt output of switch d keeps switch a open. The Efmax voltage does not effect the Efc voltage. The output voltage produces fmin in VCO.
Switch b closes and allows Efmin to change to Efc voltage.q
With switch c open, the +10 volts is routed to the control input of switch b.
With a LOW data input, the CONTROL inputs to switches c and d are zero. Switches c and d are open.
The digital data input through the op amp, IC1, changes the voltage to the VCO.
Definition
Now, when S1 is in the CONTINUOUS position, information is transmitted. The +10 volts from S1 is routed to the INPUT pins of switches c and d.
Only Efc reaches the VCO. This produces a frequency of fc, as it should be with no information signal applied (S1 in CONTROL position).
With zero volts on the CONTROL inputs, switches a and b are open. Efmax and Efmin are NOT routed to the VCO.
In this state, the voltages applied to switches a and b CONTROL inputs are 0 no matter if switches c and d are opened or closed, the DATA IN is disabled.
When S1 is in the CONTROL position, no information is to be transmitted, 0 volts is applied to the INPUT pins of switches c and d.
Definition
The switching circuit consists of four switches (a, b, c and d in IC2) as shown in the simplified schematic.
The transmitter circuit is contained on PC130-328 and consists of the components necessary to support the MC14066 analog gate and ICL8038 VCO chips.

Definition
The FM modulator circuit consists of the ICL8038 VCO modulator chip as shown in the simplified schematic.
Definition
The switching circuit produces three DC voltages according to the information digital data and if data is to be transmitted.
Switch a closes, allowing Efmax to change the Efc voltage. The output of the VCO is fmax, the third frequency.
Switch b opens, Efmin does not effect the Efc voltage.
Switch d outputs +10 volts to switch a CONTROL input and switch c outputs 0 volts to switch b (R3 drops the +10 volts).
Switch c closing places a ground in the S1, R3, switch c circuit.
Definition
With a HIGH input from IC1, both switches c and d will close.
The 0 volt output of switch d keeps switch a open. The Efmax voltage does not effect the Efc voltage. The output voltage produces fmin in VCO.
Switch b closes and allows Efmin to change to Efc voltage.
With switch c open, the +10 volts is routed to the control input of switch b.
With a LOW data input, the CONTROL inputs to switches c and d are zero. Switches c and d are open.
The digital data input through the op amp, IC1, changes the voltage to the VCO.
Definition
Now, when S1 is in the CONTINUOUS position, information is transmitted. The +10 volts from S1 is routed to the INPUT pins of switches c and d.
Only Efc reaches the VCO. This produces a frequency of fc, as it should be with no information signal applied (S1 in CONTROL position).
With zero volts on the CONTROL inputs, switches a and b are open. Efmax and Efmin are NOT routed to the VCO.
In this state, the voltages applied to switches a and b CONTROL inputs are 0 no matter if switches c and d are opened or closed, the DATA IN is disabled.
When S1 is in the CONTROL position, no information is to be transmitted, 0 volts is applied to the INPUT pins of switches c and d.
